projects.title: SciEval: evaluating K–12 science instructional materials
projects.summary: I lead task formulation, rubric co-design, and model fine-tuning for evaluating science instructional materials. SciEval provides a rubric-based benchmark with scores and evidence; Judging the Judges uses expert review to examine where model scores, explanations, and suggestions depart from instructional context.
projects.figureTitle: Connecting lesson content with evaluation criteria

projects.title: Automated formative assessment of STEM short responses
projects.summary: I developed SFRN and AsRRN to represent relationships among questions, reference responses, and student answers for automated assessment, and investigated demonstration examples for LLM assessment of science essays. Related work studies how assessed responses can be grouped to support formative feedback.

projects.title: STEM assessment datasets and human scoring rubrics
projects.summary: I contributed to the I-STUDIO and physics lab-report datasets, including rubric development and human-scoring procedures for automated assessment. Related research compares routine physics classroom grades with trained raters' judgments, showing why target labels need scrutiny and how detailed rubrics make expectations and evidence explicit before those judgments become targets for machine learning.

projects.title: LLM4Art: expert-guided art interpretation and evaluation
projects.summary: I lead application and evaluation development, translating art scholars' expertise into prompts and rubrics for visual analysis, historical context, and cultural significance. A benchmark and prototype application support comparison of model interpretations, with ongoing work on art-focused datasets, model adaptation, and educational uses.

mentor.name: Jinjun Xiong

projects.title: Human–AI collaboration: selective prediction and human deferral
projects.summary: I developed methods for automated assessment models to answer or defer to a person, including joint optimization of assessment and deferral representations. The initial work evaluates a learned deferral policy in a held-out simulation using human reference labels. Subsequent work jointly trains assessment and deferral representations across four student-answer datasets.
projects.figureTitle: Joint training of assessment and deferral

projects.title: Embodied AI: reading companions for children's AI literacy
projects.summary: I implement pedagogically structured dialogue for an LLM-powered reading robot. The feasibility study evaluates dialogue policies with simulated child profiles and an expert; it informs future studies of physical presence, turn-taking, and participation by children and adults. Related Storio studies examine bilingual conversational support in children's e-book reading: a design study with children, parents, and educators, and a separate randomized study comparing AI-guided and parent-led reading across comprehension, vocabulary, retelling, and engagement.

projects.title: AIRE: decodable story generation and evaluation
projects.summary: I lead AIRE development and co-design rubrics for phonics alignment, narrative coherence, and illustration quality with literacy experts. AIRE generates personalized decodable texts aligned with taught phonics patterns. Related work in StoryLab combines teacher-defined learning goals with children's interests to generate stories, illustrations, and vocabulary support, with teachers selecting and revising materials.

projects.title: PaiCoach: AI assessment and coaching for autism home interventions
projects.summary: I lead ASD-HI benchmark and PaiCoach model development to assess parent–child home interventions and generate feedback for specialist review. ASD-HI benchmarks communication-strategy detection and assessment. A four-family PaiCoach study found preliminary improvements under an AI-assisted workflow in which specialists corrected strategy codes and reviewed every feedback message before delivery.

projects.title: Machine reading comprehension
projects.summary: This work develops hierarchical methods for answering questions across multiple passages. Passage selection, question-relevant sentence selection, and answer extraction break the task into stages. Reinforcement learning for main-content selection examines how choosing useful evidence can improve downstream reading-comprehension models on benchmark datasets.
projects.figureTitle: From passage selection to answer extraction

projects.title: Dataflow tools for machine learning
projects.summary: A visual dataflow system makes machine-learning workflows easier to construct, execute, monitor, and reuse. Users connect operations as a directed acyclic graph in a drag-and-drop studio. The system integrates algorithm libraries with Hadoop and Spark infrastructure to support both standalone and distributed computation.

projects.title: Sentiment-aware word representations
projects.summary: This early NLP work incorporates sentiment labels into a semi-supervised language model for learning word vectors. Experiments on English and Chinese product reviews examine how semantic and sentiment information work together, studying representation choices that support review classification across the two languages.
